title: Efficient Mixture of Experts based on Large Language Models for Low-Resource Data Preprocessing

problem.claim: Data preprocessing transforms erroneous and raw data into clean data and is a cornerstone of the data mining pipeline.

gap.claim: Existing domain-specific rules and annotated-example machine-learning models are costly and time-consuming to develop for diverse downstream requirements.

contributions.claim: MELD is a universal solver for low-resource data preprocessing based on a mixture-of-experts architecture that combines and enhances domain-specific experts trained on limited annotated examples.

The paper develops expert-tuning and MoE-tuning techniques including retrieval-augmented generation, meta-path search for data augmentation, expert refinement, and information-bottleneck-based router training.
The paper provides theoretical results claiming that MELD's mixture of experts is superior to a single expert and that its router can dispatch data to the appropriate experts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on 19 datasets covering 10 data-preprocessing tasks.
The authors report that MELD outperforms state-of-the-art methods in effectiveness and efficiency.
The authors report that MELD can be fine-tuned in a low-resource environment such as a local, single, low-priced 3090 GPU.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data preprocessing is foundational to the data mining pipeline.
Diverse downstream requirements make handcrafted rules and annotated-example machine-learning models costly and time-consuming.
The paper introduces MELD, a mixture-of-experts solver for low-resource data preprocessing.
MELD is fine-tuned using retrieval augmentation, meta-path data augmentation, expert refinement, and router training based on information bottleneck.
The paper reports theoretical support, experiments across 19 datasets and 10 tasks, effectiveness and efficiency gains, and low-resource fine-tuning feasibility.

source_observation.claim: Combining domain-specific experts trained on limited annotations can support low-resource data preprocessing.

interpretation.claim: A mixture-of-experts design may reuse specialized capabilities while reducing dependence on large labeled datasets.

application.claim: For heterogeneous preprocessing tasks with scarce labels, consider routing inputs among specialized experts instead of training one general model alone.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which task types, data conditions, or routing failures may limit this approach.

source_observation.claim: The reported method combines retrieval augmentation, data augmentation, expert refinement, and router training.

interpretation.claim: Low-resource performance may depend on coordinating several tuning mechanisms rather than on the mixture-of-experts architecture alone.

application.claim: When adapting expert systems with limited annotations, evaluate retrieval, augmentation, expert refinement, and routing as interacting components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not isolate the contribution of each tuning technique.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, task definitions, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical assumptions or proof details.
The abstract does not report resource costs beyond the example of a 3090 GPU.
